proposals.before: Book of Jin, scroll 118—Annals eighteenth.
proposals.after: Book of Jin, scroll 118—Records eighteenth.
proposals.reason: 載記 designates the Jinshu records of non-Jin regimes, not the annalistic 紀; Annals mistranslates the heading.

proposals.before: Southern Yan defectors arrived—Zhong the prince of Beidi, Wang Yi of Jiyang, and Shi duke of Gaodu.
proposals.after: Murong Chao's minister of education and Prince of Beidi Zhong, Right Pushe and Prince of Jiyang Yi, and Duke of Gaodu Shi all fled hither.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names 慕容超 and 嶷; the idiomatic line omits Murong Chao and misreads 嶷 as Wang Yi.

proposals.before: He hurled Yao Chong, Di Bozhi, Liancheng Manwei, and Yang Fosong—forty thousand riders—at Bobo.
proposals.after: He hurled Yao Chong, Di Bozhi, Lian Manwei, and Yang Fosong—forty thousand riders—at Bobo.
proposals.reason: 斂曼嵬 is Lian Manwei, distinct from 斂成 already rendered Liancheng.

proposals.before: Right Vice Director Wei Hua and others remonstrated, saying, "If the Chariot-and-Cavalry General moves lightly, he will collapse without battle, and he may not even reach Wei’s camp. May Your Majesty consider it."
proposals.after: Right Vice Director Wei Hua and others remonstrated, saying, "If the imperial carriage and cavalry move lightly, they will collapse without battle, and they may not even reach Manwei’s camp. May Your Majesty consider it."
proposals.reason: Cheqi qingdong refers to Xing light movement, not a Chariot-and-Cavalry General; Wei camp is Lian Manwei camp, not Wei.

proposals.before: Right Vice Director Wei Hua and others remonstrated, saying, "If the Chariot-and-Cavalry General moves lightly, he will collapse without battle, and he may not even reach Wei’s camp. May Your Majesty consider it."
proposals.after: Right Vice Director Wei Hua and others remonstrated, saying, "If the imperial carriage and cavalry move lightly, they will collapse without battle, and they may not even reach Manwei’s camp. May Your Majesty consider it."
proposals.reason: Same errors as the idiomatic line: cheqi is the moving host/carriage, and Wei is Manwei, not Wei.

proposals.before: Huan Qian's noble name seduced wavering Jin troops.
proposals.after: Huan Qian was an aristocrat of the eastern Yangzi; his retainers filled Jing and Chu, and Jin officers and soldiers all harbored thoughts of defection.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line invents seduction by a noble name and drops retainers in Jing-Chu and officers harboring defection.

proposals.before: He toured the imperial park until dusk and aimed for Pingzhuo Gate.
proposals.after: He toured from Chaomen to the civil-military park until dusk and aimed to enter by Pingshuo Gate.
proposals.reason: Pingshuo Gate is Pingshuo, not Pingzhuo; Chaomen and the civil-military park are dropped.

proposals.before: Xing roamed from Chaomen to the civil-military park; reaching dusk he returned intending to enter through Pingzhuo Gate.
proposals.after: Xing roamed from Chaomen to the civil-military park; reaching dusk he returned intending to enter through Pingshuo Gate.
proposals.reason: Pingshuo is Pingshuo, not Pingzhuo.

proposals.before: Cao Chi, Cao Yun, and Wang Sifo shepherded refugees inland—Fo to Zhuang wetlands, the Caos to Chencang.
proposals.after: Xing officers Cao Chi, Cao Yun, and Wang Sifo each led several thousand households fleeing Bobo inland; Xing settled Fo among the Huangshan wetlands, and Chi and Yun at Chencang.
proposals.reason: Huang is Huang, not Zhuang; several thousand households and Xing as settler are omitted.

proposals.before: Yao Xing promoted Bi to minister of education, attendant-in-ordinary, and grand general.
proposals.after: Yao Xing appointed Bi Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Palace Attendant, and Grand General.
proposals.reason: Shangshu ling is not Minister of Education (situ).

proposals.before: At this Xing appointed Bi minister of education, palace attendant, grand general.
proposals.after: At this Xing appointed Bi Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Palace Attendant, and Grand General.
proposals.reason: Shangshu ling is misrendered as minister of education.

proposals.before: Yao Xing spurned Bi and sent Suo Leng to coax Gangui.
proposals.after: Xing did not follow; he made his Grand Master of Ceremonies Suo Leng Grand Commandant and concurrent Interior Secretary of Longxi to soothe and induce Gangui.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line drops Taichang, Taiwei, and concurrent Longxi interior secretary.

proposals.before: Liang Guoer banqueted inside his living tomb west of Pingliang.
proposals.after: At the time the western Hu Liang Guoer built a longevity tomb at Pingliang; he often brought his wives and concubines into the tomb to drink and feast, and when flushed with wine he mounted the spirit couch and sang.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English relocates 于平涼 as west of Pingliang, drops 西胡, and omits the tomb feasts and singing.

proposals.before: He died past eighty a decorated frontier general.
proposals.after: For campaigns front and rear he repeatedly earned great merit; Xing made him General Who Guards the North and enfeoffed him Baron of Pingyu; aged over eighty he died.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits the 鎮北將軍 appointment, 平輿男 enfeoffment, and stated age.

proposals.before: He sent Jianwei Zhao Kun with five thousand cavalry as the vanguard, followed by Yang Boshou with infantry. Former General Yao Hui and Left General Yao Wenzong entered through Jiashan, Yao Song, Inspector of Qinzhou and General Who Garrisons the West, entered Yangtou Pass, and Right Guard Hu Yidu came out from Yinmi through Qiancheng to attack Yang Sheng.
proposals.after: He sent Jianwei Zhao Kun with five thousand cavalry as the vanguard, followed by Yang Boshou with infantry. Forward General Yao Hui and Left General Yao Wenzong entered through Jiashan, Yao Song, Inspector of Qinzhou and General Who Garrisons the West, entered Yangtou Pass, and Right Guard Hu Yidu came out from Yinmi through Qiancheng to attack Yang Sheng.
proposals.reason: 前將軍 is Forward General, not Former General.

proposals.before: Twenty-four late ministers joined sacrifices at Yao Chang's shrine.
proposals.after: He also issued an edict assigning the former Chancellor Yao Xu, Grand Steward Yao Shuode, Grand Mentor Yao Min, Grand Marshal Yao Chong, Minister over the Masses Yin Wei, and others among twenty-four men to paired sacrifice at Chang's temple.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops the five named honorees.

proposals.before: Yao Bi framed Wenzong before crown prince Hong.
proposals.after: Yao Wenzong enjoyed Yao Hong's favor; Yao Bi deeply hated him, accused Wenzong of resentful words, and used Attendant Censor Lian Taosheng as witness.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line invents a framing before Hong and omits Hong's favor, the charge, and Lian Taosheng.

proposals.before: Palace guards under Yao Shao sealed the inner compound.
proposals.after: Pacification-Army General Yao Shao, Palace Attendant Ren Qian, Right Pushe Liang Xi, Champion Yao Zan, Jingzhao Yin Yin Zhao, and Assistant-State General Lian Manwei jointly commanded the forbidden troops and guarded within.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops five named inner-palace commanders.

proposals.before: Yao Xing spared Bi but stripped the Secretariat.
proposals.after: Because Bi combined civil and martial talent, Xing could not bear to apply the law; he dismissed him as Director of the Imperial Secretariat and had him go to his manor as general and duke.
proposals.reason: 尚書令 is the Secretariat directorate, and general and ducal rank at the manor are retained.

proposals.before: Xing because Bi joins civil martial could not bear apply law dismissed minister of education retaining general duke returning manor.
proposals.after: Xing, because Bi combined civil and martial talent, could not bear to apply the law; he dismissed him as Director of the Imperial Secretariat, retaining general and duke, and sent him back to his manor.
proposals.reason: 尚書令 is not minister of education.

proposals.before: They demanded execution; Yao Xing refused.
proposals.after: Yi, Hui, and Hui's younger brother Chen and others jointly memorialized blaming Bi and begging that he be delivered to the penal law; Xing refused.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits the named memorialists 懿、恢及弟諶.

proposals.before: Wei sought renewed marriage ties.
proposals.after: At that time Wei sent envoys to pay court to Xing and also requested a marriage alliance.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops 時、遣使聘於興, so the embassy to Xing and the request for marriage disappear.

proposals.before: Dou Wen and Wang Bi had urged deposing Bi in secret.
proposals.after: Earlier, Grand Minister of Agriculture Dou Wen and the Minister of Education's Left Chief Clerk Wang Bi both submitted secret memorials urging Xing to depose and replace the heir.
proposals.reason: 勸興廢立 is a request that Xing change the heir, not that they depose Yao Bi; 司徙 is the office 司徒. The idiomatic line also collapses offices and misidentifies the target.

proposals.before: King Wen's transformation applied punishment to few wives;
proposals.after: King Wen's transforming influence set the example from his own wife;
proposals.reason: 刑于寡妻 is the Shijing idiom of moral example beginning with one's wife, not criminal punishment of wives.

proposals.before: Rage jailed Yao Xiang at Xingcheng while Bi took thirty thousand west.
proposals.after: In great anger he then arrested Xuan at Xingcheng, threw him into prison, and sent Bi with thirty thousand men to garrison Qinzhou.
proposals.reason: 宣 is Xuan, not Xiang; the idiomatic line also drops 下獄 and turns 鎮秦州 into an unstated 'west'.

proposals.before: Xing went Beidi Bi halted Three Trees dispatching Bi and Liancheng Manwei toward Xinping Xing returned Chang'an.
proposals.after: Xing went to Beidi; Bi halted at Three Trees; he dispatched Bi and Lian Manwei toward Xinping; Xing returned to Chang'an.
proposals.reason: 斂曼嵬 is Lian Manwei; 'Liancheng' invents a place-name element not in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Sima Xiuzhi, Sima Zongzhi, Qiao Prince Wensi, Xincai Prince Daoci, Ma Jing, General Who Pacifies the Caitiffs and inspector of Liangzhou, Lu Gui, General Who Supports the State and grand administrator of Jingling, and Lu Fan, General Who Pacifies the Caitiffs and grand administrator of Nanyang, fled to Yao Xing.
proposals.after: Xiuzhi, Zongzhi and the others then fled to Xing together with the Prince of Qiao, Wensi; the Prince of Xincai, Dao Ci; Ningshuo General and Liangzhou Inspector Ma Jing; Fuguo General and Jingling Prefect Lu Gui; and Ningshuo General and Nanyang Prefect Lu Fan.
proposals.reason: 宗之 is Lu Zongzhi, not Sima Zongzhi; 甯朔 is not 'Pacifies the Caitiffs'; titles are assigned to the wrong men.

proposals.before: Xiuzhi and others reaching Chang'an Xing told them: "Liu Yu reveres serves Jin emperor how could instantly flaw?"
proposals.after: When Xiuzhi and the others reached Chang'an, Xing said to them: "Liu Yu honors and serves the Jin emperor; how could there already be a deficiency?"
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English is word-for-word and ungrammatical; the Chinese asks whether Liu Yu's service of the Jin emperor already shows a lack.

proposals.before: Xiuzhi said: "Your servant earlier descended capital Prince Langye Dewen weeping told Your servant Liu Yu supplies attends lord above stingy thin extraordinary deep.
proposals.after: Xiuzhi said: "When your servant previously went down to the capital, the Prince of Langye, Dewen, told your servant in tears: 'Liu Yu's provisioning and attendance on His Majesty are extraordinarily mean and thin."
proposals.reason: The quoted complaint of Dewen is collapsed into broken glosses and loses speaker boundaries.

proposals.before: Yao Xing meant to seat Xiuzhi on the Jingzhou frontier.
proposals.after: Xing intended to appoint Xiuzhi Inspector of Jingzhou and entrust him with affairs of the southeast.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits 荊州刺史 and 東南之事, which the literal still records.

proposals.before: Xiuzhi chose raiding Xiangyang instead.
proposals.after: Xiuzhi firmly declined, asking to join Lu Zongzhi and others in harassing Xiangyang and the Huai and Han.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic drops Lu Zongzhi and the Huai-Han objective.

proposals.before: He named Xiuzhi southern guardian and Yangzhou shepherd.
proposals.after: He then appointed Xiuzhi General Who Guards the South and Inspector of Yangzhou, and Zongzhi and the others likewise received appointments.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic fuses titles and omits 宗之等並有拜授.

proposals.before: Xing mournful changed expression summoning Yao Zan Liang Xi Yin Zhao Liancheng Manwei Consultation Hall secretly plotting seize Bi.
proposals.after: Xing's expression turned sorrowful; he summoned Yao Zan, Liang Xi, Yin Zhao, and Lian Manwei to the Consultation Hall and secretly plotted to seize Bi.
proposals.reason: 斂曼嵬 is Lian Manwei, not Liancheng Manwei.

proposals.before: I should deeply restrain feeling through ritual, and thereby quiet the altars."
proposals.after: He ought himself to suppress emotion for ritual's sake, and thereby quiet the ancestral altars."
proposals.reason: 自宜 advises Hong in the third person, not a first-person 'I should'.

proposals.before: We others because Duke Guangplain reason sunk body rebel rhythm.
proposals.after: We have, because of the Duke of Guangping, sunk ourselves in treason.
proposals.reason: Guangplain is a corruption of Guangping (廣平).

proposals.before: Yet We knew not Your demise not also fitting!"
proposals.after: Yet We did not know you—was Our ruin not fitting!"
proposals.reason: 亡也 refers to Fu Jian's fall, not Yin Wei's demise; 卿 is the unrecognized talent.

proposals.before: Yao Chang favored erudite courtier Duan Keng.
proposals.after: Duan Keng of Fengyi was artful by nature; Yao Chang prized his broad learning and drew him in as Attendant-in-ordinary.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops Fengyi, the judgment that Duan was crafty, and the office 侍中.

proposals.before: Yin Wei anchored Yao Xing's victory over Fu Deng.
proposals.after: After Yao Chang died, Yin Wei joined Yao Xing in destroying Fu Deng; completing Xing's enterprise was entirely Wei's doing.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic sentence omits 萇死 and the historian's judgment that Xing's achievement was all Wei's strength.

proposals.before: Upon death Xing deeply mourned him posthumous Sikong posthumous title Loyal Accomplished Marquis.
proposals.after: Upon death Xing deeply mourned him, posthumously granted Situ (Minister of Education; 司徙 for 司徒), posthumous title Loyal Accomplished Marquis.
proposals.reason: 贈司徙 is Situ (司徒), not Sikong (司空); the literal English names the wrong office.

decisions.reason: 載記 is the Jinshu rubric for non-Jin regimes, not the annalistic 紀; Annals is a mistranslation of the heading.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 載記第十八

decisions.reason: The Chinese names Murong Chao (慕容超) and Prince of Jiyang Yi (濟陽王嶷); the original omits Chao and misreads 嶷 as Wang Yi.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 慕容超司徒、北地王鐘，右僕射、濟陽王嶷，高都公始，皆來奔。

decisions.reason: 斂曼嵬 is Lian Manwei; Liancheng invents a 成 not present in this name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 輔國斂曼嵬

decisions.reason: In context of 車駕, 車騎輕動 is the imperial carriage and cavalry moving lightly, not a Chariot-and-Cavalry General; 嵬營 is Manwei's camp.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 若車騎輕動，必不戰自潰，嵬營亦未必可至

decisions.reason: The same two errors as the idiomatic line: 車騎 is the moving host, and 嵬 is Manwei, not Wei.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 若車騎輕動，必不戰自潰，嵬營亦未必可至

decisions.reason: The original invents seduction by a noble name and drops 江左貴族, 部曲遍于荊、楚, and 晉之將士皆有叛心.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 謙，江左貴族，部曲遍于荊、楚，晉之將士皆有叛心。

decisions.reason: 平朔門 is Pingshuo Gate, not Pingzhuo; 朝門 and 文武苑 are omitted in the original.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 興從朝門游于文武苑，及昏而還，將自平朔門入。

decisions.reason: 平朔 is Pingshuo, not Pingzhuo.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 將自平朔門入

decisions.reason: 湟山澤 is the Huangshan wetlands, not Zhuang; the original also drops 各將數千戶 and Xing as the one who settled them.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 興將曹熾、曹雲、王肆佛等各將數千戶避勃勃內徙，興處佛於湟山澤，熾、雲于陳倉。

decisions.reason: 尚書令 is Director of the Imperial Secretariat, not Minister of Education (司徒).

sourceWitness.excerpt: 興以弼為尚書令、侍中、大將軍

decisions.reason: 尚書令 is misrendered as minister of education in the literal line.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 興以弼為尚書令、侍中、大將軍

decisions.reason: 興不從 is refusal of the advice, not merely 'spurning Bi'; the line must keep 太常, 太尉, and concurrent 隴西內史.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 興不從，以其太常索棱為太尉，領隴西內史，綏誘乾歸。

decisions.reason: 于平涼 locates the tomb at Pingliang, not west of it; 西胡 and the tomb feasts and singing are omitted.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 時西胡梁國兒于平涼作壽塚，每將妻妾入塚飲宴，酒酣，升靈床而歌。

decisions.reason: The original omits 鎮北將軍, 平輿男, and the campaigns that earned the honors, keeping only a vague death past eighty.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 前後征伐，屢有大功，興以為鎮北將軍，封平輿男，年八十餘乃死。

decisions.reason: 前將軍 is the Forward General title, not Former General.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 前將軍姚恢

decisions.reason: The original drops the five named honorees 姚緒、姚碩德、姚旻、姚崇、尹緯 among the twenty-four.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 故丞相姚緒、太宰姚碩德、太傅姚旻、大司馬姚崇、司徒尹緯等二十四人配饗於萇廟

decisions.reason: 文宗 was favored by Hong; Bi hated him and accused him of resentful words with 廉桃生 as witness—not a framing staged before Hong.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 姚文宗有寵于姚泓，姚弼深疾之，誣文宗有怨言，以侍御史廉桃生為證。

decisions.reason: Six named officers jointly commanded the forbidden troops; collapsing them into 'palace guards under Yao Shao' omits the other five.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 撫軍姚紹及侍中任謙、右僕射梁喜、冠軍姚贊、京兆尹尹昭、輔國斂曼嵬並典禁兵，宿衛於內。

decisions.reason: 尚書令 is the Secretariat directorate, and 以將軍、公就第 retains general and ducal rank at the manor; the original omits both the motive and the retained ranks.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 興以弼才兼文武，未忍致法，免其尚書令，以將軍、公就第。

decisions.reason: 尚書令 is not minister of education; the literal line must name the Secretariat directorate.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 免其尚書令

decisions.reason: The memorialists are named 懿、恢及弟諶; 請致之刑法 is delivery to penal law, not necessarily execution.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 懿、恢及弟諶等皆抗表罪弼，請致之刑法，興弗許。

decisions.reason: 時魏遣使聘於興，且請婚 is an embassy to Xing plus a marriage request; 'renewed' is invented and the embassy is dropped.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 時魏遣使聘於興，且請婚。

decisions.reason: 勸興廢立 urges Xing to change the heir, not to depose Yao Bi; 王弼 is a separate clerk, and 司徙左長史 is the Minister of Education's Left Chief Clerk.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 大司農竇溫、司徙左長史王弼皆有密表，勸興廢立。

decisions.reason: 刑于寡妻 is the Shijing idiom of moral example beginning with one's wife, not criminal punishment of wives.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 文王之化，刑于寡妻

decisions.reason: 宣 is Xuan, not Xiang; 下獄 and 鎮秦州 are omitted when the original says only 'west'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遂收宣於杏城，下獄，而使弼將三萬人鎮秦州。

decisions.reason: 斂曼嵬 is Lian Manwei; Liancheng invents a 成 not in the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遣弼及斂曼嵬向新平

decisions.reason: 宗之 is Lu Zongzhi, not Sima Zongzhi; 甯朔將軍 is Ningshuo, not Pacifies the Caitiffs; titles belong to Ma Jing, Lu Gui, and Lu Fan as paired in the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 休之、宗之等遂與譙王文思，新蔡王道賜，甯朔將軍、梁州刺史馬敬，輔國將軍、竟陵太守魯軌，甯朔將軍、南陽太守魯范奔於興。

sourceWitness.excerpt: 琅邪王德文泣謂臣曰：'劉裕供禦主上，克薄奇深。

decisions.reason: 鎮南將軍 and 揚州刺史 are distinct offices, and 宗之等並有拜授 is omitted by 'southern guardian and Yangzhou shepherd'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 乃以休之為鎮南將軍、揚州刺史，宗之等並有拜授。

decisions.reason: 斂曼嵬 is Lian Manwei, not Liancheng Manwei.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 召姚贊、梁喜、尹昭、斂曼嵬於諮議堂

decisions.reason: 自宜 is third-person advice to Hong, not a first-person 'I should'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 自宜深抑情禮，以甯宗社。

decisions.reason: 廣平公 is the Duke of Guangping; Guangplain is a corruption, and 陷身逆節 is sinking into treason.

decisions.reason: 朕不知卿 is Fu Jian's failure to know Yin Wei; 亡也 is Jian's own ruin, not Wei's demise.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 萇死，緯與姚興滅苻登，成興之業，皆緯之力也。

decisions.after: Upon death Xing deeply mourned him, posthumously granted Situ (Minister of Education), posthumous title Loyal Accomplished Marquis.
